response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan, AVG(f.rebrate * 1.0 / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), s AS (SELECT g.*, AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER () AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(cnt) AS total_distinct_orders, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM s WHERE cnt > avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: The per-group ratio is the average of the row-level rebrate/feerate. Rows with a NULL rebrate or feerate are ignored. A feerate of 0 is treated as missing (NULLIF) to avoid division by zero.

Distinct orders are counted by orders.recordvault. A NULL timespan, if present, is treated as its own group. The cross-group average count is the unweighted mean of the per-group counts over all groups, before filtering.

alternatives.interpretation: The group ratio is the ratio of averages, AVG(rebrate)/AVG(feerate), instead of the average of row-level ratios.
alternatives.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan, AVG(f.rebrate) * 1.0 / NULLIF(AVG(f.feerate), 0) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), s AS (SELECT g.*, AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER () AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(cnt) AS total_distinct_orders, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM s WHERE cnt > avg_cnt
